title: Text generation on a Galaxy S23 Ultra
subtitle: Generic long-text tests—not measured podcast-script speed or quality.
tokens_per_second_explanation: Tokens are text pieces, not words; ‘reads’ processes prompts, ‘writes’ generates new text.
label_fairness: Reading/writing are useful stage metaphors, not human comprehension or correctness claims.

tier_choice.why: Closest available test to reading a substantial source and generating a longer response. Still a generic task, not a podcast-script measurement.
tier_choice.statistic: Exact median of five loaded-route long requests per row; initial loading and the first short request are excluded. Display reads to one decimal and writes to two; retain exact medians below.
tier_choice.loaded_route_plain_words: The model and runtime stay loaded. Each request starts with fresh conversation/cache state and processes the whole prompt again. No previous answer or prompt cache is reused; reset/session creation is timed separately, outside these rates.
tier_choice.three_tiers: Short, medium and long are different fixed requests, not interchangeable repetitions. Compare the same tier across routes; do not pool them or disguise their range as uncertainty. Long ran last in each sustained campaign, so tier effects and operating conditions are not isolated.

rows.writes_missing_reason: Registry withholds normalized decode rate: Genie does not define whether the first generated token is included. Raw profile rates exist but must not fill this cell.

comparability.all_seven: All seven use the identical canonical long workload bytes and generation ceiling, with no input truncation. Side-by-side route observations on the same logical task are legitimate, not a controlled architecture/hardware ranking.
comparability.same_artifact_pairs: The Gemma LiteRT CPU/GPU pair, Qwen CPU/OpenCL pair and LFM CPU/OpenCL pair each share their own model artifact, rendered prompt and input token IDs. No such exact-artifact pair spans all three Gemma backends.
comparability.not_identical: Across families, tokenizers and chat templates differ. Gemma HTP uses a different mobile-QAT checkpoint/deployment; even its input-token stream differs from LiteRT. Outputs and stop lengths can differ between paired backends. Same task does not mean identical computation or completion.
comparability.no_script_claim: These measurements do not time the app's outline/chapter pipeline, test script quality, or show how quickly an accepted podcast script will be produced.

htp_registry_audit.recorded_outcome: Physical HTP execution completed the canonical campaign without CPU fallback markers. All five long outputs hit the output ceiling and failed narrow sanity for severe repetition collapse; short/medium passed that corruption check. Normalized decode rate is null because first-token inclusion is undefined, independently of the output failure. No quality acceptance is recorded.
No Qwen HTP row in this seven-route registry. Its listed routes are CPU and OpenCL GPU, not NPU. Absence does not establish that no other experiment attempted HTP or that it succeeded/failed.
No LFM HTP row in this seven-route registry. Its listed routes are CPU and OpenCL GPU, not NPU. No HTP performance or fidelity outcome can be attributed to this registry.

caveats: Tokens are not words, and different tokenizers divide text differently. Reads and writes are separate metrics; do not combine them into one speed score or compare their numeric magnitudes as equal work.

Five-request medians are observed sustained-campaign values, not thermally normalized. Gemma LiteRT CPU/GPU, Qwen CPU/GPU and LFM GPU ended at thermal status 3; Gemma HTP and LFM CPU ended at status 4.
Output sanity checks corruption/repetition, not truth, grounding, prose quality or acceptance. The NPU row's severe long-output collapse is visible in the row, not hidden behind its prefill rate.

LFM CPU long outputs reached the valid output ceiling; LFM GPU long outputs reached EOS with a different length. Qwen CPU/GPU completion lengths also differ. Rates are not equal-length script latency comparisons.
Isolated GPU-private memory was not measured; process PSS/RSS is not total GPU memory. HTP-private allocations are also unavailable. No memory or energy-efficiency claim follows.
OpenCL GPU offload still uses CPU orchestration and some CPU operations. GPU/NPU labels identify the deployed neural route, not an entirely accelerator-only application.
Normalized decode rates exclude the first generated token from count and interval. Gemma HTP lacks that definition, so its writes cell stays null, not zero or a substituted raw rate.
what_stands_out: On the long workload, Gemma LiteRT-LM GPU recorded higher prefill and decode medians than its same-artifact CPU route.
omission_reason: None: all seven registered runtime/backend routes are distinct and retained, including the HTP observation with its recorded repetition failure.
presentation: Use a separate LLM table, grouped by model, with plain reads/writes columns and units. Render null as words. Keep the generic-test subtitle and NPU failure visible; link registry IDs in details. Do not mix with TTS RTF or label a fastest script writer.

sources.owner_records: Owning result.json and campaign README paths are listed under sources for each registry ID; inspected for 0025/0027/0031/0033/0035.

activity: Read-only repository inspection and checks on retained observations; no phone, inference, builds, registry regeneration or repository edits.
